15: {33} And we read in Bereshit Rabbah (30:4): “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Anyone whose name is doubled exists in two worlds, in this world and in the world to come. It is written, "These are the generations of Noah, Noah" (Gen. 6:9). It is written, "Abraham, Abraham" (Gen. 22:11). It is written, "And He said: Jacob, Jacob" (Gen. 46:2). It is written, "Moses, Moses" (Ex. 3:4). It is written, "These are the generations of Peretz, Peretz" (Ruth 4:18). And it is written, "Samuel, Samuel" (1 Sam. 3:10). They said to him: But is it not written, "Terah, Terah" (Gen. 11:27)? He said to them: In the end he repented. Abraham did not depart from the world until he received the tidings that his father had repented, as it is said, "And you shall come to your fathers in peace" (Gen. 15:15).” Abraham said before the Holy Blessed One: Master of the World, by all the mitzvot and good deeds I have stored up in this world, I will merit the world to come, while my father inherits Gehinnom, because he served idols, as it is said, "Terah, the father of Abraham..." (Josh. 24:2). The Holy Blessed One said to him: By your life, he will repent before his death, as it is said, "And they came as far as Haran and they settled (va-yeshvu) there" (Gen. 11:31). Do not read va-yeshvu, "they settled," but va-yashuvu, "they returned," for they returned in repentance. Therefore his name was doubled, "These are the generations of Terah, Terah," in two worlds. So we see that children atone for the sin of their parents.
